name: PlantUML Interactive Desktop
description: Intent architecture for PlantUML Interactive Desktop — a Windows application enabling drag-and-drop PlantUML diagram editing with free-position canvas, bidirectional code-canvas sync, and one-click export.

elements.name: Individual Developer
elements.description: Primary user persona: individual developer who needs intuitive PlantUML diagram editing on Windows without manual environment setup

elements.name: Need for Intuitive PlantUML Editing on Windows
elements.description: Existing PlantUML editors are either web-based, code-only, or require complex setup. Developers want a native Windows experience with visual drag-and-drop.

elements.name: Current Web App Limitations
elements.description: The existing Flask web application: (1) requires browser plus running server, (2) no drag-and-drop interaction, (3) requires manual Java installation, (4) right-click modal-based editing limits UX

elements.name: Windows Desktop PlantUML Editor with Drag-and-Drop
elements.description: Deliver a native Windows application that allows users to edit PlantUML diagrams by directly dragging elements onto a free-position canvas, rearranging them visually, and connecting them with drag-to-link interactions

elements.name: One-Click Install with Zero Manual Setup
elements.description: User downloads a single installer, clicks Next-Next-Install-Finish, and the application is ready. JRE and PlantUML JAR are downloaded automatically on first launch.

elements.name: Visual Drag-and-Drop Editing Experience
elements.description: Users can drag elements from a component palette onto a canvas, reposition them freely, reconnect arrows by dragging handles, and see real-time PlantUML code synchronization.

elements.name: Free Positioning Canvas
elements.description: The canvas allows users to place elements at any (x, y) coordinate. Position is NOT encoded in the exported .puml file since PlantUML is an auto-layout engine.

elements.name: Last Operation Wins for Bidirectional Sync
elements.description: When both canvas and code editor are modified concurrently, the last-touched side (by timestamp) determines the authoritative state.

elements.name: Tolerant Import with Unsupported Block Passthrough
elements.description: When importing PlantUML files containing unsupported diagram types, the parser parses what it can and stores unrecognized text as opaque UnsupportedBlock nodes.

elements.name: Full Activity Diagram Support
elements.description: Must support: Activity (color/URL/break/detach), Start/Stop/End, If/Else/Elseif, While/EndWhile, Repeat, Fork, Switch, Note, Group/Partition, Title, Connector, Merge, Arrow labels.

elements.name: Free-Form Canvas with Drag-and-Drop (All Three Levels)
elements.description: Canvas must support Level A (palette to add), Level B (rearrange), Level C (reconnect arrows). Elements freely positionable.

elements.name: One-Click Export to Valid .puml
elements.description: Export button produces a valid PlantUML .puml file. Position information excluded per free-position principle.

elements.name: One-Click Export to PNG via Java Rendering
elements.description: Export PNG invokes java -jar plantuml.jar -tpng on the backend.

elements.name: Import Existing .puml Files with Grid Layout
elements.description: Importing a .puml file parses text into AST and renders on a default grid layout.

elements.name: Bidirectional Code-Canvas Real-Time Sync
elements.description: Canvas edits update code (debounced 200ms). Code edits re-parse and update canvas. Last-op-wins resolves conflicts.

elements.name: No Manual Java Installation Required
elements.description: End users must never be asked to install Java, Python, or any runtime manually.

elements.name: No Manual Python Installation Required
elements.description: Python backend must be PyInstaller-compiled into a standalone executable.

elements.name: Exported .puml Must Be Valid PlantUML
elements.description: Every exported .puml file must be parseable by standard PlantUML tooling.

elements.name: Windows-Only Target (Installer for Windows 10/11 x64)
elements.description: The initial deliverable targets only Windows 10/11 64-bit via NSIS installer.

elements.name: Create PlantUML Diagram
elements.description: End-to-end user workflow: start app, add elements on canvas, arrange by drag, connect by drag, preview, export .puml or .png

elements.name: PlantUML Diagram Model (AST)
elements.description: The authoritative in-memory representation of a PlantUML diagram as a typed AST.

elements.name: AST Data Model
elements.description: TypeScript types and model library defining node types, edge types, container hierarchy, and DiagramModel. All other components depend on this.

elements.name: PlantUML Parser Engine
elements.description: Parses PlantUML text into DiagramModel AST. Uses stack-based nesting tracking. Tolerant parsing with UnsupportedBlock fallback.

elements.name: PlantUML Generator Engine
elements.description: Generates valid PlantUML text from DiagramModel AST. Tree-walk with depth-tracked indentation.

elements.name: ReactFlow Canvas Engine
elements.description: ReactFlow-based free-position canvas with custom nodes, connection handles, container nesting, drag-to-reorder, drag-to-connect.

elements.name: Component Palette
elements.description: Left-side panel listing draggable element types. Supports drag-to-canvas creation.

elements.name: Ace Code Editor Integration
elements.description: Ace editor wrapper with PlantUML syntax highlighting and line markers.

elements.name: Bidirectional Sync Engine
elements.description: Manages canvas-code sync: version tracking, timestamp conflict detection, fingerprint position preservation, cycle prevention.

elements.name: Electron Desktop Shell
elements.description: Electron main process: window management, native menus, file dialogs, subprocess management, JRE download, auto-update.

elements.name: Python Render Backend
elements.description: PyInstaller-compiled Flask app exposing render endpoints: POST /render (SVG), POST /renderPNG (PNG), GET /health.

elements.name: Windows 10/11 x64 PC
elements.description: User's Windows desktop computer. Target deployment environment.

elements.name: Electron Runtime
elements.description: Chromium-based desktop application runtime.

elements.name: JRE (jlink Minimal Runtime)
elements.description: Minimal Java runtime (~40MB) with java.base and java.xml modules. Downloaded on first launch.

elements.name: PlantUML JAR
elements.description: PlantUML v1.2022.5+ JAR file (~20MB) for rendering SVG/PNG. Downloaded on first launch.

elements.name: PlantUML File (.puml)
elements.description: Standard .puml file format. Import source and export target.

elements.name: PNG Image File
elements.description: Rendered diagram as PNG image. Export-only artifact.

elements.name: NSIS Installer (.exe)
elements.description: Windows NSIS installer by electron-builder. Contains Electron and PyInstaller'd backend. JRE/PlantUML downloaded at first launch.

elements.name: AC-001: Installation and First Launch
elements.description: Verification that installer requires no manual steps beyond Next-Next-Install-Finish.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-001
testcases.description: User completes installation with default options and app starts with auto-download of rendering dependencies
testcases.Input: Double-click PlantUML-Editor-Setup-x.x.x.exe then accept defaults then Finish
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Installation completes with no Java or Python prompts
2. First launch shows download progress dialog (~60MB total)
3. On completion, empty activity diagram (start->stop) renders
4. JRE at APPDATA\PlantUML-Editor\jre\
5. plantuml.jar at APPDATA\PlantUML-Editor\plantuml\
6. plantuml-backend.exe visible in task manager

elements.name: AC-002: Drag from Palette to Add Element (Level A)
elements.description: Verification that dragging an Activity from palette onto canvas creates a new node and updates code.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-002
testcases.description: User drags Activity from palette to canvas blank area
testcases.Input: Left-click-hold Activity in palette then drag to canvas at (300, 200) then release
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Drag preview follows mouse
2. Node appears at drop position with default text
3. Code editor shows ':new activity;' at correct indentation
4. Node position.x=300, position.y=200
5. order index correct within parent scope

elements.name: AC-003: Drag to Reorder (Level B)
elements.description: Verification that dragging an element across containers updates model hierarchy and PlantUML text.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-003
testcases.description: User drags Activity into an if/else container's then-branch
testcases.Input: Drag Activity A onto If container then-branch highlight zone then release
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. If container highlights drop zone during drag
2. Activity A appears inside then-branch
3. Activity A.parentId = then-branch ContainerNode id
4. Code shows Activity A inside if block with correct indentation
5. order index sequential within then-branch

elements.name: AC-004: Drag Handle to Connect (Level C)
elements.description: Verification that dragging from a connection handle creates an arrow edge.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-004
testcases.description: User drags from Activity A bottom handle to Activity B top handle
testcases.Input: Hover Activity A to show handle then drag to Activity B top then release on highlight
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Dashed line follows mouse during drag
2. Activity B top highlights as target
3. Solid arrow A->B appears after release
4. Edge model: source=A.id, target=B.id
5. Code shows arrow at correct position

elements.name: AC-005: Free Position Persistence Across Code Edits
elements.description: Verification that user-positioned elements retain coordinates when code triggers re-parse.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-005
testcases.description: User positions three activities, edits one in code
testcases.Input:
1. Place A at (300,150), B at (150,400), C at default
2. Modify C text in code editor
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. After code edit, A and B positions unchanged (fingerprint match)
2. C text updates, position retained
3. No elements flicker or jump to grid

elements.name: AC-006: Bidirectional Sync with Last-Op-Wins
elements.description: Verification that concurrent canvas and code edits resolve by last-touch-first.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-006
testcases.description: Concurrent canvas drag and code edit
testcases.Input: Drag Activity A on canvas while simultaneously typing in code editor
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Last-modified (by timestamp) wins
2. No infinite update loop
3. syncState version counters increment correctly
4. lastGeneratedPuml guard prevents cyclical re-sync

elements.name: AC-007: One-Click Export to .puml
elements.description: Verification that export produces a valid PlantUML file via native save dialog.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-007
testcases.Input: Click Export then choose directory then save as test.puml
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Native Save dialog shows 'PlantUML Files (*.puml)' filter
2. File exists at chosen path
3. File has valid @startuml...@enduml
4. Rendered by plantuml.com matches diagram structure
5. No position coordinates in file

elements.name: AC-008: Import .puml with Grid Layout
elements.description: Verification that importing a .puml file correctly parses and renders on grid.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-008
testcases.Input: File then Import then .puml then select test.puml then Open
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Canvas displays parsed elements on grid layout
2. All supported node types identified
3. Unsupported features as grey placeholder blocks
4. Nested structures (if-in-if) correctly rebuilt
5. Code editor shows original text
6. All elements freely draggable

elements.name: AC-009: Tolerant Parsing of Incomplete PlantUML
elements.description: Verification that importing incomplete PlantUML does not crash.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-009
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. App does not crash
2. Canvas shows parsed portions
3. Unparsed text preserved in code editor
4. Error block on canvas for unparseable section

elements.name: AC-010: One-Click Export to PNG
elements.description: Verification that PNG export invokes Java rendering and saves the image.

testcases.name: ACCEPT-010
testcases.Input: Click Export PNG then choose directory then save
testcases.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Rendering completes within 5 seconds
2. PNG matches diagram structure
3. File opens in Windows Photo Viewer
4. Backend java -jar plantuml.jar -tpng invoked successfully
